His shoulder looked angry. Raw tension threaded through the entire arm. “Jesus, man,” Jake muttered. “You look like shit.” Leon grunted in response, shifting his weight to pull himself off the floor, leaning heavily against the cabinet as he tried taking the weight off his shoulder. “Don’t sugarcoat it.” Jake crossed the room in three strides, crouching to examine the cuff. “What the hell happened to you?” Leon exhaled a humorless laugh and rattled the cuff lightly. “Apparently, my hiding skills got me promoted from gen jockey. Welcome to my new desk job.” Jake tugged at the metal, bracing one foot on the cabinet as he tried to get the chain to snap. It creaked lightly against the cabinet handle, but didn’t budge. “You’ve gotta be kidding me. He cuffed you to a freaking filing cabinet?” “Didn’t even get a chair. The working conditions here suck.” “Don’t you guys usually have keys for these things?” Leon pushed his bangs back with one hand, yanking the cuff sharply in irritation and wincing as it bit into him again. “Pretty sure the Doctor pocketed them while he was searching me. I was a little... out of it. ” He gestured vaguely toward the wall with his free hand. “Didn’t exactly get the luxury of staying conscious through most of the decision-making process.” Jake huffed through his nose. “Well, that’s comforting.” He reached for the screwdriver clipped to his belt and wedged the flat end into the hinge between the cuff and the cabinet. The metal resisted, but he leaned in harder, tongue between his teeth, working the angle. It wasn’t the cleanest method, but maybe if he could just pry the lip— Leon’s body jerked suddenly beside him. “Hold on — don’t—” The air had shifted again — that metallic taste returned — and in the moment, Jake had completely missed it. Leon surged forward, shoving Jake back with his free just as the cabinet lit up like a bug zapper. Electricity danced along the edges, funnelled straight through the cuff and into Leon’s arm. He arched violently, mouth open in a scream that caught midway, choking on itself as his body seized and bucked against the restraint. Jake hit the floor with a hard thud, palms scraping against the tile. His screwdriver skittered off to the side, spinning once before vanishing beneath a rusted gurney. “ Shit— ” He twisted, scrambling to push upright just in time to see Leon slam against the cabinet, back arching, head snapping back. The sparks died off, and for a moment, all Jake could do was stare. Leon sagged forward, the cuff dragging taut as he crumpled, then steadied himself with one trembling arm. His eyes were open — unfocused, distant, breath caught somewhere between a gasp and a choke. One hand curled against his vest, nails biting fabric as he struggled to ride out the recoil. “Leon?” No answer. Jake took a step forward. Leon lifted a shaky hand — not up, but out. Just a small wave. A breathless “wait.” A hold. Jake froze. Leon knelt fully, head bowed, breathing shallow and quick. His shoulders rocked faintly with the rhythm of his pulse. After a few moments, he dropped back against the cabinet again, letting the cuff yank taut above him with a hiss. “...What the fuck was that?” Jake asked, quieter now. Almost like the walls might answer. Jake’s eyes traced the line between Leon’s arm and the cuffs, up through the metal cabinet, and around the room. Sparks still popped gently between pieces of furniture across the room, like static creeping along a thundercloud’s edge. Jake followed the line — from one overturned tray to a chrome IV stand, then up the cabinet where Leon’s arm trembled just shy of collapse. “Holy shit, it’s focusing the static blasts, isn’t it?” “Yeah,” Leon rasped, settling himself off his knees and sitting back against the cabinet, “Yeah, I may have noticed.” “You were trying to tell the others not to bring the chase down this way. That’s what I heard earlier.” Leon’s head thunked against the cabinet as he panted. “It’d be nice if I could get a warning out before the world goes white again. They’re moving around so fast... there’s no time.” “There’re easily 3 generators within radius of here, too. Fucking hell...” Leon nodded, eyes distant. Jake was catching up fast, drawing the same conclusion. Even if they managed to warn the others off, eventually they would HAVE to come back this way. There was simply no avoiding it. Jake idly fiddled with his toolbelt, trying to think of a plan. “There’s gotta be a way to break this.” He crouched beside the cuff again, eyeing the hinge. “I’ve pried a lock off a hook tower before. This is just... smaller.” He flexed his hand, already tingling from the earlier zap. “If I had something better than a screwdriver—” His breath caught. The hook. His mind skipped back — to the moment in the hallway. The sabotaged hook. The thrashing figure on Herman’s shoulder. He hadn’t known who it was. Hadn’t stopped to check. “ Fuck, ” Jake whispered. “That was you. I—” He stood up fast, hands bracing on his head. “If I hadn’t—shit—if I hadn’t taken that hook down—” Leon waved him off dismissively. “Don’t waste time feeling bad about something that worked. It slowed him down, gave you space. He just got creative. Guilt won’t help us now.” “...But —" “It was the right call in the moment. Seriously. I would have done the same. What we need now is some way to break these off.” Jake swallowed the guilt back and tried to focus. He was right. It wasn’t serving anyone right now.
